reason: Base UI draws Checkbox and Radio as a span, so shadcn's disabled:opacity-50 (a :disabled selector) never matches and a disabled control stays fully opaque upstream; rhea reads [data-disabled] instead, which is what the utility means. An upstream defect, not a rhea value. Same as foundation's.

The preset is generated with rtl:false, so its paddings and radii are physical (pl-/pr-, rounded-l-) and do not mirror under dir=rtl; the layer-3 rules are logical. The section proves DirectionProvider renders, not a value. Same as foundation's.

A preset app's globals.css carries no .cn-* rules, so the cn-input-otp class the shadcn component keeps is unstyled there; style-rhea.css's `.cn-input-otp { gap-2 }` is rhea's own value and the system keeps it. Same as foundation's.

The shortcuts contain ⌘, which is in neither Inter build: the reference app falls back through next/font's Inter Fallback and the preview through Inter Variable plus the Pretendard Hangul fallback, so the glyph advance differs by ~0.5px. Font stack, not a value. Same as foundation's.

rhea's generated questionnaire.tsx carries `sm:min-h-8` on QuestionnaireActions while the shadcn base component (which registry/ui follows) carries `sm:min-h-9`. The preset bakes the value into the component as a utility, so no layer-3 rule can reach it and one shared set of TSX cannot hold both. The row and everything it stretches are 4px taller here. Same shape as foundation's, with rhea's number.

rhea gives the switch thumb `shadow-sm`, which the preset's own switch.tsx carries as a utility next to `ring-0`; Tailwind composes both into one box-shadow. registry/ui's Switch keeps shadcn's `ring-0` but has no shadow utility (TSX holds no visual values), and `ring-0` alone composes box-shadow in the utilities layer, which beats any layer-3 rule in layer(base). The cause is the shared TSX, not a rhea value, and this run does not change registry/ui.

Dark mode only: Tailwind sorts rhea's dark: colours (dark:bg-transparent on the outline button, dark:aria-invalid:border-destructive/50 on the checkbox) after the state utilities that have no dark counterpart (aria-expanded:bg-muted, aria-invalid:aria-checked:border-primary), so upstream an open outline trigger and an invalid checked checkbox lose their state colour in dark. rhea keeps the state colours; reproducing the ordering would delete the signal. Same as foundation's.
